results.notes:
Shared turn record built behind MODEL_GATEWAY_SHARED_TURN_RECORD (default off; parsed with mp_contracts::loop_fold::switch_from, the same strict parser run_control uses). With it off nothing is written or read, so behaviour is unchanged.

What it does when on:
- sse.rs: one call-in after record_chat_turn, skipped for waived turns. ZDR turns return earlier and never reach it. mirror_chat_turn spawns a best-effort write of {run_id, skill_ids} to Redis at mp:gw:turn:{org}\x1f{user}\x1f{request_id}, TTL 24 h (TURN_TTL).
- http_routes.rs: ingest_feedback calls ChatTurnRegistry::adopt_shared after the existing ZDR guard (require_non_zdr_durable_mutation). On a local miss it reads the caller's own shared record into the local map, then the unchanged sync resolve_feedback_target runs. A miss leaves today's turn_not_rateable / run-only behaviour. Ownership is still verified by Session Core.
- stream_buffer.rs: StreamBufferStore gains kv_set and kv_get, run under the existing stream-buffer Breaker (250 ms op timeout, 5 s cooldown). The in-memory backend does nothing there. Log lines carry the op name, not the key.
- chat_turn_registry.rs: shared_turn_key (refuses blank, oversized or separator-bearing parts), SharedTurnStore trait (native async fn, pub(crate)) so the mirror is tested against a fake, mirror_turn, lookup_shared_turn, adopt_shared. PreviousTurnRegistry stays local.

New tests: shared_turn_key_is_identity_scoped, switch strictness, cross-replica round trip, other user or tenant misses, ids-only record plus 24 h TTL, local record not overwritten, corrupt or run-less record is a miss, unusable turn not mirrored, in-memory store mirrors nothing, and two feedback-route tests (resolves on replica B through the shared record; another caller cannot resolve it).

CRLF and LF preserved: stream_buffer.rs stays CRLF; the other three stay LF. rustfmt was run only on chat_turn_registry.rs (LF).

depth_findings.text: Until S3, chained rows are never purged (Purge skips chain_seq IS NOT NULL), so the audit table grows unbounded once the flag is on; S3's chain-safe purge must ship before long-running use.

A rolling deploy lets an old-image replica insert an unchained row with ingested_at just before an org's activated_at, so it is silently classed legacy_unchained and never chained; a stop-the-world image swap or an activation grace window is needed before the flag is switched on.
CatchUp runs only at boot; rows written while the switch is off on a replica that stays up are chained only at the next restart, so a periodic catch-up sweep may be wanted.

results.notes:
The code, the unit tests and every new switch default (off) are in place. The Postgres-backed chain tests were never run, because there is no local Postgres and I may not run docker. The lead must run them through the harness before this is treated as verified.

Built:
- Migration 007_audit_chain.sql, embedded in migrate.go:
  - Adds the five nullable chain columns, the unique index uq_audit_events_org_chain, the table audit_chain_heads, and the guard trigger audit_events_guard.
  - The guard blocks UPDATE and DELETE except the one transition that chains an unchained row, or a transaction that set audit.maintenance='on'.
  - Revert file: internal/store/migrations/revert/007_audit_chain.down.sql.
- store.New(pool, ...Option) with WithChain(). The unchained insert path is the same statement as before, now a shared insertAuditSQL constant.
- internal/store/chain.go:
  - Chained path: one transaction takes the head lock, spot-checks the tip hash, inserts, hashes from the read-back row, then updates row and head in a pgx batch.
  - A replay or conflict commits and falls to resolveAuditConflict unchanged.
  - A tip mismatch marks the head broken, counts it once, logs it, and still appends.
  - CatchUp chains only unchained rows with ingested_at at or after the org's activated_at, as chain_mode 'catchup', in 500-row transactions.
  - The details guard (D7 observe mode) counts ok, oversize (over 8 KiB) or denied_key; it never rejects.
- Four metrics: audit_core_chain_appends_total{result}, ..._head_lock_wait_seconds, ..._chain_broken_total, audit_core_details_guard_total{result}.
- main.go: AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED, then boot catch-up before the subscriber starts. A catch-up failure is logged and boot continues.
- Purge now runs in a transaction with audit.maintenance on and skips chained rows (chain_seq IS NULL only). Without this the new trigger would break retention, and deleting a chained row would break its chain.
- Tests: chain_insert_test.go (new) plus the guard, loadConfig and compose-default tests listed above. Existing DB tests in store_test.go and session_core_replay_test.go now use execMaintenance for their UPDATE and DELETE.
